title: Privacy-Preserving Hybrid CNN-Based RF Fingerprinting for Open-Set IoT Device Authentication in Dynamic Wireless Environments
problem_statement: RF fingerprinting systems in IoT environments face significant challenges due to open-set recognition, channel variability, noise interference, and adversarial spoofing attacks. Existing models degrade severely under changing environmental conditions such as Rayleigh and Rician fading, making real-world deployment unreliable.
motivation: With the rapid expansion of IoT devices in smart cities, healthcare, and industrial automation, secure device authentication is critical. Traditional cryptographic authentication methods are computationally expensive for low-power IoT devices, motivating lightweight RF-based identification systems.
methodology: We propose a hybrid deep learning framework combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with prototype learning and contrastive consistency regularization. The model learns robust RF embeddings invariant to channel variations. A prototype memory bank is maintained for each device class, and open-set detection is performed using distance-based thresholding in embedding space. Additionally, data augmentation simulates real-world channel distortions.

system_architecture.feature_extraction: CNN-based multi-layer feature extractor for raw IQ signal processing
system_architecture.embedding_space: Prototype-based metric learning with cosine similarity scoring
system_architecture.regularization: Consistency loss between augmented signal views

dataset.description: RF signal dataset collected from 300 IoT devices including sensors, smart meters, and embedded controllers.
dataset.environment: Signals captured under controlled and real-world conditions including Rayleigh fading, Gaussian noise, and Doppler shifts.
dataset.preprocessing: IQ normalization, noise filtering, and segmentation into fixed-length windows

experimental_setup.optimizer: Adam optimizer with learning rate scheduling
experimental_setup.loss_functions: Cross-entropy loss + contrastive loss + prototype alignment loss

limitations: Performance decreases in extreme low SNR environments and requires further optimization for ultra-low power edge devices.
future_work: Extend the framework to federated RF learning across distributed IoT networks, integrate transformer-based signal encoders, and optimize deployment on edge AI chips such as NVIDIA Jetson Nano and ARM Cortex-M series.
